16:I[12454,["/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/08cykig6vtx_p.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/07qi2okp-.yp9.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0frujd.eyhz4o.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0n4z.7yu76je-.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0otjhi71vbmnx.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0j1uy9t~zxcf0.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/1304s0wcp2kce.js"],"WeeklyView"]
17:T893,FROST has two main ingredients: real-anchored utility estimation and conditional filtering.

For utility estimation, each training step draws both a real batch and a synthetic batch. The method maintains an exponential moving average of gradients from recent real batches, which serves as a smoothed reference direction for the real-data objective. Each synthetic sample is then scored by the alignment between its gradient and this real-gradient reference. The intuition is straightforward: if a synthetic sample pushes parameters in a direction similar to what recent real data prefers, it is more likely to be useful; if it points away, it is more likely to be harmful or off-distribution.

The second ingredient is conditional filtering. The authors argue that per-sample gradient utility is noisy, so filtering every batch aggressively can remove useful supervision. They first aggregate utilities at the batch level and compare the batch mean against recent history to determine whether the batch falls inside a moderate utility band. Batches inside the band are kept as-is. Only out-of-band batches trigger sample-level filtering, where interquartile-range thresholds are used to retain or discard examples within the batch. This design is meant to avoid overreacting to stochastic gradient noise while still rescuing good samples from otherwise weak batches.

Relative to common synthetic-data selection methods, FROST differs in three ways. It does not require a separate pretrained feature extractor for fidelity/diversity scoring, so it avoids expensive offline preprocessing of the full synthetic pool. It does not need a held-out validation set or an external judge, because the real training stream itself provides the anchor. And it is online: utility is recomputed as the model evolves, rather than assigned once in a static preprocessing stage.

From a pretraining perspective, the hidden assumption is that an EMA of real-data gradients is a stable proxy for the target objective. That seems plausible in moderate-scale fine-tuning, but it is less obvious in large mixed-corpus pretraining where gradient noise, domain conflict, and real/synthetic ratios can be very different.18:T621,The paper evaluates FROST on image classification, LLM fine-tuning for text-to-SQL, and a large industrial ads re-ranking system. On the public benchmarks, it filters out roughly 20% to 30% of synthetic data while outperforming training on the full synthetic pool.

The reported gains are 0.58% to 1.14% absolute accuracy improvement across three synthetic image generators, and 0.9% improvement on text-to-SQL fine-tuning. The industrial result is more telling in practical terms: using the full noisy synthetic pool causes a 0.211% relative NE regression compared with the real-only baseline, while FROST turns that into a 0.096% relative NE improvement. The authors note that gains around 0.02% are already considered meaningful in mature production recommenders, so the industrial effect size is not trivial.

Methodologically, the matched-drop-ratio comparison is important. The paper compares selection methods under the same synthetic-data discard rate, which makes the gains more attributable to better selection rather than simply using less data. Also worth checking is the ablation on batch-level gating plus sample-level filtering versus always-on per-sample filtering, since that is the part intended to control gradient-noise sensitivity.

The main caveat is scope. The LLM experiment is a downstream fine-tuning task, not large-scale language-model pretraining. The paper does not establish that real-anchored gradient utility remains stable or cost-effective for next-token pretraining with large synthetic corpora or reasoning-heavy synthetic mixtures.19:T4d9,For a skim read, start with the Introduction and Method to understand the logic of real-anchored utility and conditional filtering. Then read the text-to-SQL experiment and the main ablations. Around 20 to 30 minutes should be enough to decide whether the idea is portable to your own data pipeline.

Focus on four details. First, inspect how utility is computed in practice: full gradients, projected gradients, or some approximation. That determines scalability. Second, check how the real-gradient EMA is updated and stabilized, because the whole method depends on the anchor being reliable. Third, read the calibration rule for batch means and the IQR-based sample filtering, since that is where the paper tries to avoid over-filtering under noisy gradients. Fourth, look for behavior across different drop ratios, synthetic-data quality levels, and training stages.

If your interest is pretraining data rather than downstream fine-tuning, treat this as a prototype idea: use training signals instead of static data features to select synthetic data. Before scaling it up, the open questions are compute overhead, gradient approximation quality, and whether the real-gradient anchor remains meaningful under multi-domain mixed training.1a:T7c5,The formulation starts from minimum-token segmentation with a vocabulary budget. Each document is represented as a byte-level DAG whose edges are candidate substring occurrences. Byte edges are always available; multibyte edges are available only if the corresponding string is selected into the vocabulary. Given a vocabulary, minimum-count encoding is just a shortest path in the usable subgraph. The coupling difficulty is that selecting one token type enables all of its occurrences across the corpus.

The main idea is an occurrence-level Lagrangian relaxation. Each candidate occurrence gets a non-negative price lambda_e. On the document side, segmentation becomes a shortest-path problem with edge costs increased by these prices. On the vocabulary side, each token type accumulates the total bid of all its priced occurrences, and the lower bound subtracts the sum of the top-K bids allowed by the vocabulary budget. This yields a computable lower bound without a generic LP solver: shortest paths per document plus a global top-K selection over token bids. The paper argues that maximizing over prices recovers the LP relaxation, while validity of the reported bound is checked separately with an exact integer checker.

A useful extension is the boundary-licence formulation. Instead of only comparing the two endpoints—fully regex-constrained versus fully unrestricted—the method allows a budget on how many vocabulary entries may cross regex cuts. That produces a compression frontier and makes the design question continuous: how much compression can be recovered by permitting a small number of cross-boundary tokens.

The paper also keeps compression and prediction separate. Compression is analyzed through certified token-count intervals. Prediction is evaluated on held-out data with an explicit vocabulary and decoding protocol, because unrestricted vocabularies change token frequencies, context granularity, and effective predictability, not just sequence length.1b:T52e,The headline result on English Wikipedia is a certified boundary tax: regex boundaries increase the optimal token count by 28.3% to 36.8%. That is a large effect, showing that pre-tokenization boundaries materially constrain the compression optimum. BPE is only 2.1% above the constrained lower bound, which supports the claim that under a fixed regex regime BPE is already close to the best achievable compression. But BPE is 10.9% above the unrestricted lower bound, which explains why boundary-relaxing methods can still obtain substantially shorter sequences. These are not contradictory findings; they refer to different optimization problems.

The multilingual study covers 12 languages. Unrestricted fitted dictionaries compress better, but they have higher mean test bits-per-byte in every language. With independent tuning and evaluation seeds, the direction remains in 11 of 12 languages. This is the most practically relevant result for LM researchers: fewer tokens do not necessarily mean easier prediction or lower held-out loss.

The boundary-licence experiments are also important, even if the abstract only hints at them. They show how compression improves as a limited number of cross-boundary vocabulary entries are allowed, which is more informative than a binary constrained-versus-unrestricted comparison.1c:T470,The study frames PPT as a two-stage autoregressive NLL training process. A model is first trained on a small synthetic or control corpus D_PPT, producing an initialization θ_PPT, and then trained on a standard PT corpus D_PT. This is compared against a PT-only model trained from random initialization. The experimental grid varies four axes: the PPT task, the PT mixture, model scale, and PT token budget. The five PPT tasks include two formal-language tasks, including k-Shuffle Dyck, two structured synthetic tasks without formal grammars, and an in-domain text control sampled from the PT corpus. The PT mixtures include C4, Marin, SmolLM3, and OLMo3, covering pure or web-heavy text, filtered mixtures with code and math, and a STEM-weighted mixture. A frozen Qwen3-0.6B-Base encoder provides clean text states. Response states are corrupted in continuous space, and a bidirectional Transformer denoiser predicts clean states through velocity regression. The model also learns a token decoder, so the final response tokens are emitted in parallel. ELF-REG adds REPA+REG. REPA aligns intermediate denoiser states with hidden states from a frozen Qwen3-1.7B-Base AR teacher, using a learned projector and cosine loss at matching token positions. REG adds a global teacher-derived target: the last content-token state from the teacher is standardized, corrupted, and denoised as an extra token. This token exchanges information with text through self-attention and receives velocity-regression and REPA supervision. At inference time, the teacher and projector are removed; text states and the REG token start from noise, and only text is decoded. The paper also studies early stopping by decoding intermediate clean predictions before the full denoising trajectory finishes.23:T747,MoSAR, short for Mixture of Semantic Attention Regimes, inserts a lightweight router on the post-RoPE Q/K pathway. The router is bilinear and conditions on both queries and keys, rather than routing only one side. That choice is important: routing only queries gives row-wise structure, and routing only keys gives column-wise structure, but neither can localize useful two-dimensional regions of the attention matrix before dense similarities are computed. With both sides routed, the interaction between token i and token j selects a regime.

Each semantic regime defines a distance gate g(d). The gate is not just a simple exponential decay. It has a near-distance plateau where RoPE interactions are largely preserved, a transition region with smooth attenuation, and a low-relevance region where interactions become small enough to approximate away. This avoids the semantic discontinuity of hard local masks and makes approximability an outcome of the learned geometry.

The routing is input-conditioned and applied after positional encoding, so regime selection depends on contextual token representations that already carry positional structure. That is why the paper uses the term semantic regimes: locality is not determined by distance alone. MoSAR-Cost adds an explicit pressure toward shorter expected reach, biasing the router toward cheaper regimes and turning the quality-efficiency trade-off into a trainable objective.

Relative to prior efficient attention methods, the differences are clear. It does not predefine a sparse pattern; it predefines a set of decay laws and lets the data choose among them. It does not start by deleting edges; it first learns continuous attenuation and then exploits low-value regions for approximation. And it treats efficient attention as a geometry-learning problem rather than only an operator-design problem.24:T5f3,The main study uses 500M-parameter models trained from scratch and compares dense RoPE, fixed-locality baselines, MoSAR, and the cost-aware MoSAR-Cost. The headline result is that adaptive controlled decay outperforms both dense RoPE and fixed locality among the evaluated variants at 4096 and 8192 tokens, with MoSAR achieving the best perplexity in those long-context settings. The gains appear to be concentrated where long-range structure matters, which is aligned with the method’s goal.

The more interesting result is the inference-time approximation study. The authors replace soft mixture routing with deterministic top-1 routing at inference, effectively discretizing the learned geometry. This substantially reduces expected normalized reach while keeping perplexity competitive under length extrapolation. That suggests the learned regimes are not merely a training-time regularizer; they induce a geometry that can be compressed into a cheaper routing policy. MoSAR-Cost pushes the trade-off further toward lower reach, with some language-modeling cost, making the quality-versus-compute curve explicit rather than reporting a single operating point.

The most useful ablations are likely the ones on one-sided versus two-sided routing, number of regimes, the role of smooth transition regions, strength of cost regularization, and extrapolation behavior. The key question is not only whether perplexity improves, but whether perplexity, reach, and approximation error move in a stable and interpretable way.25:T412,Start with the introduction and lock onto the paper’s reframing: the target is not a better hand-designed sparse pattern, but a learned decay geometry over attention interactions. Then go to the method section and focus on three pieces: the definition of a semantic regime, the bilinear query-key router, and the MoSAR-Cost objective. It is worth understanding why routing is applied after RoPE rather than before it.

In the experiments, prioritize figures and tables that show perplexity across context lengths, expected or normalized reach, and the gap between soft mixture routing and deterministic top-1 routing. If time is limited, try to answer three questions: do the learned regimes actually separate into different locality behaviors, do those behaviors vary with layer and token semantics, and is the inference-time discretization loss small enough to matter in practice. Around 35 to 50 minutes should be enough for a solid skim. For replication judgment, the appendix on implementation details and extra ablations is necessary.26:T421,The analysis has three parts. First, it characterizes the population-optimal UDM predictor. Because uniform corruption mixes preserved tokens and random vocabulary tokens, every subset of observed positions defines a hypothesis about which context tokens are reliable. Time does not create new hypotheses; it reweights them through the noise level, with a signal-to-noise quantity such as rho_t = K alpha_t / (1 - alpha_t) controlling how much the observed context should be trusted. Second, the work studies the empirical finite-data oracle. In language data, the discrete sequence space is huge, and training examples are typically far apart. A corrupted sequence therefore remains closer to its original clean sequence than to competing examples over most noise levels, causing the posterior to concentrate and reducing the effect of time-dependent reweighting. Third, it derives a bound linking empirical time sensitivity to a post-corruption separation margin. The bound weakens near the high-noise endpoint, where multiple hypotheses become plausible.27:T4d5,LAVOIR builds on the Laya/Jev interface for typed decisions. The original input contains the question type, instruction, option markers, and the state. LAVOIR appends a slot block for candidate missing information. A single forward pass returns both the decision distribution and a predicted VOI score for each slot. The model keeps Laya’s ModernBERT-large decision head and adds a zero-initialized segment embedding so that, when no slots are present, the logits match Laya exactly in fp32. The VOI head reads each slot representation together with features of the current decision distribution and predicts a scalar value. It is a small MLP with about 0.27M parameters, LayerNorm, a 256-unit GELU hidden layer, and a scalar output. A Gini-based cap constrains the predicted value by the maximum expected gain of a calibrated posterior, which prevents the model from over-asking when it is already confident. Training labels are produced without human annotation: schema rules define the gold decision for complete profiles, an LLM verbalizes messages and answers, exact posteriors are computed by enumeration, and realized gains are measured as the increase in the model probability assigned to the gold decision after asking a slot.28:T4d9,LUDI changes the UDLM recipe in two places. First, it introduces a less uniform loss. The usual KL objective for UDLM matches the reverse transition to the exact posterior, but part of the objective encourages the prediction distribution to remain too uniform. With a large vocabulary, this weakens the clean-token signal and hurts few-step reverse generation. The authors simplify and approximate the original objective, decompose it into three terms, and remove the term that pushes predictions toward uniformity. The resulting loss drives each reverse transition more directly toward the clean token. Second, LUDI adds per-token time embeddings. A global diffusion time does not tell the model which individual positions are likely corrupted. Token-level time embeddings provide corruption hints for each position, letting the model identify reliable condition tokens and uncertain target tokens. This enables confidence-based sampling similar in spirit to masked diffusion models: generate easy or high-confidence tokens first, then use them as context for harder positions. Unlike MDLMs, LUDI keeps the uniform vocabulary prior rather than a mask-token prior. Unlike AR models, it does not force a strict left-to-right generation order.29:T534,The method, REST (REpresentation-Supervised Thoughts), augments the standard final-answer cross-entropy with four differentiable losses on the latent thought itself. The theoretical setup argues that CE on the final answer does not penalize bad intermediate representations as long as the correct answer remains sufficiently likely, so recursive systems can accumulate representational errors over rounds and across agents.

REST targets four properties. Causality requires the thought to preserve information needed to reproduce the correct output. Minimality pushes it to discard information irrelevant to that output. Separability prevents semantically distinct inputs, especially those with different output distributions, from collapsing to similar latent thoughts. Stability encourages the thought to reflect the distribution over plausible outputs rather than a single sampled answer trace. These losses are added to CE with tunable weights.

Implementation-wise, the paper studies both a multi-agent latent recursive system and a single-agent variant where a model feeds its own hidden states back as the next reasoning step. Importantly, REST does not change the architecture or inference procedure; it only changes the training objective. That makes the paper more about missing supervision than about a new system design.2a:T432,The evaluation spans MATH500, GPQA-Diamond, MedQA, AIME2025/2026, LiveCodeBench-v6, and MBPP+. Under matched training budget, identical training data, and the same latent budget, REST improves over CE-only by +3.5 points on average in the multi-agent setting and +3.3 in the single-agent setting. The best configurations reach +7.5 and +6.5 points, respectively. For a skim-level read, these are the main numbers to retain.

The paper also reports that REST decodes 15.4% more tokens on average at inference. The authors attribute this to a higher rate of convergence to a final answer. That is an interesting trade-off: better latent supervision improves accuracy, but not necessarily by reducing visible decoding cost in the current setup.

The analysis sections matter more than usual here. The paper claims that CE-only systems exhibit thought collapse and retention of irrelevant information, while REST-trained systems better satisfy the targeted properties. Those diagnostics are central to judging whether the method is doing more than adding another auxiliary loss.2b:T4e1,The model follows the standard LoopLM decomposition: a Prelude P, a shared recurrent core F, and a Coda C, written as C ∘ F^K ∘ P during training. At inference, the number of recurrent applications can be changed to r. The study first uses minimalist LoopLMs under controlled pretraining settings, fixing effective training depth while varying the number of physical layers and recurrent loops. This isolates the effect of recurrence from total training depth. The paper then studies two design axes. The first is where non-recurrent computation should be placed. Output-side non-shared blocks help preserve knowledge behavior, especially when the model is under-unrolled, while input-side non-shared computation tends to help reasoning extrapolation. The second is how the recurrent core should be conditioned. Initial-state injection can hurt knowledge robustness when over-parameterized. The proposed history-state injection instead conditions on relative changes from intermediate states, giving the recurrent core access to trajectory information. Timestep conditioning lets the shared core behave differently at different loop indices. A lightweight channel-wise parameterization combines history-state injection and timestep conditioning.2c:T42a,The experiments compare inference budgets below, at, and beyond the training horizon on both knowledge and reasoning tasks. A simple LoopLM can continue improving beyond its training horizon, and some configurations outperform non-recurrent counterparts under comparable training compute. The behavior is task-dependent: reasoning tasks can benefit from extra loops, while knowledge tasks may degrade. Harder reasoning examples do not consistently gain more from additional recurrence, which weakens the view that recurrence automatically allocates computation to difficult cases. Models with the same effective training depth but different physical-depth and loop-count configurations show different scaling curves. Ablations show that output-side non-recurrent blocks improve knowledge robustness under shallow unrolling, input-side blocks are more useful for reasoning extrapolation, and the joint conditioning design outperforms BaseLoop and the individual conditioning variants under extended inference budgets, with Fig. 7(c) serving as the central comparison.2d:T8ee,方法分成 TES 和 ACS 两条线。

TES，token-error supervision，在原生 router 之外增加一个轻量的 error head。这个 head 以共享的 token 表示为输入，为每个 expert 预测一个误差分数。然后用 native affinity 对这些 expert-wise error 做加权聚合，使聚合后的预测误差去拟合该 token 实际观察到的 next-token cross-entropy。训练好后，TES 不只是做一个辅助预测；它还在路由阶段把预测误差反馈到 expert 排序里：论文采用从 native affinity 中减去一个按比例缩放的 log-error 项，再做 top-K 选择。直观上，若某 expert 对当前 token 预测误差更高，就降低它被选中的相对优先级。这个设计保留了原有 top-K 稀疏预算，也不改 expert aggregation policy。

ACS，affinity-concentration supervision，则更克制。它不引入额外 head，也不在推理时改路由公式，而是直接用 realized token loss 去监督已选 expert 的归一化 affinity 概率的平方项。作者的解释是，这相当于根据 token loss 去调节路由分布该更尖锐还是更平坦：某些 token 上应更集中地押注少数 expert，另一些 token 上则不应过度集中。它是一个 headless 的对齐方式，参数和推理开销都更小。

监督目标上，论文主要用 Itakura–Saito divergence，也试了 ENLL。理论分析部分给出的关键结论是：对 TES 而言，两者都把聚合误差预测推向相同的期望目标，但对 LM 优化的梯度影响不同。若预测误差与真实误差一致，IS 不改变原始 CE 更新；ENLL 会相对放大低损失 token 的梯度权重。这个分析很重要，因为它说明“把 token error 接进 router”不是只有一个实现细节问题，而会改变训练动力学。

和已有方法相比，这篇工作不是重新设计一个全新 router，也不是增加更复杂的 expert selection 网络，而是在保留原生 MoE 结构和 top-K 预算的前提下，把 token-level error 作为显式监督接入路由。它的优点是兼容现有 backbone，改动小；局限是监督信号来自 realized CE，本身受当前模型状态影响，可能更适合 fine-tuning 或后期 router 校正，而未必直接适合早期大规模预训练。2e:T942,The method has two variants: TES and ACS.

TES, or token-error supervision, augments the native router with a lightweight error head. From the shared token representation, the head predicts an error score for each expert. These expert-wise predicted errors are then aggregated using the native affinity weights, and the aggregate is trained to match the realized next-token cross-entropy for that token. At inference and training time, TES does more than auxiliary prediction: it modifies expert ranking by subtracting a scaled log-error term from the native affinity before top-K selection. Intuitively, experts predicted to incur higher error are down-weighted in the routing decision. This preserves the original sparse execution budget and the architecture’s native expert aggregation policy.

ACS, or affinity-concentration supervision, is the lighter alternative. It adds no extra head and does not alter inference-time routing with an extra transformation. Instead, it directly supervises the squared probabilities of the normalized selected-expert affinities using the realized token loss. The effect is to encourage the routing distribution to become sharper or flatter depending on token difficulty. In other words, it shapes how concentrated the native router should be, without introducing a separate error predictor.

For supervision, the paper mainly uses Itakura-Saito (IS) divergence and also studies ENLL. The theoretical section is important. For TES, both objectives target the same expected token-error quantity, but they induce different optimization dynamics. When predicted and observed token error match, IS leaves the original CE update unchanged, whereas ENLL relatively upweights lower-loss tokens. That is a meaningful distinction: adding token-error supervision is not merely an auxiliary loss choice, but a change to how gradients are distributed.

Relative to prior MoE routing work, the contribution is not a new router architecture. It is a way to keep the native MoE design and top-K budget intact while explicitly supervising routing with token-level error. That makes the proposal easy to graft onto existing backbones. The likely limitation is that realized CE is itself model-state dependent, so the method may be better suited to fine-tuning or late-stage router correction than to the earliest phases of large-scale pretraining.2f:T525,Experiments are run on two backbones, Granite 3.1 and OLMoE-1B, across four multiple-choice QA benchmarks. The main comparisons are against standard CE fine-tuning and a parameter-matched Dual Affinity baseline.

On Granite, ACS-IS improves average accuracy by 2.1 points over CE fine-tuning with frozen native affinity. TES-IS improves over the parameter-matched Dual Affinity baseline by 2.3 points on Granite and 0.5 points on OLMoE, averaged across the four benchmarks. Under stronger supervision, TES reaches a 2.94-point gain on Granite ARC-Challenge.

These results support two conclusions. First, direct token-error supervision can improve routing in practice, not just in theory. Second, the better mechanism depends on the backbone and task: some settings benefit more from explicit error prediction, others from headless affinity shaping. The paper also keeps the native top-K execution budget unchanged in all variants, which matters for deployment realism.

From a pretraining perspective, the empirical scope is still limited. The paper does not show large-scale pretraining loss curves, routing stability during long runs, or how expert specialization evolves under these objectives. The evidence is therefore best read as a routing-supervision prototype rather than a validated MoE pretraining recipe.30:T515,For each output position, the model runs an internal decision process over a hidden state h, a fast-weight memory M, and a counter of Think steps. The latent policy chooses among Think, Recall, and Exit. Think applies a shared Transformer block again, increasing effective depth without adding new block parameters, and writes the resulting state into memory. Recall reads from the same memory and injects the retrieved representation into the current hidden state. Exit stops the inner loop and emits the next token through the language-model head. This differs from external-memory agents, where memory is usually read back as text or context, and from looped latent-reasoning models, where the loop has no native memory read action. The training method, Counterfactual Policy Distillation, branches every allowed action for one step at each latent state, including Exit, and scores the branch by the change in the gold token log-probability. The resulting cost-charged, signed gain supervises the action policy. In addition, recall improvements on positive-advantage trajectories are differentiated through the fast-weight memory, assigning credit to earlier Think writes. This is important because a memory system must learn both what to retrieve and what to store before retrieval becomes useful.31:T777,方法是一个两阶段、两次前向的 SFT recipe。输入是 prompt-response 样本，prompt 始终可见，只对 response token 做 mask。训练时先采样噪声水平 t，再额外采样一个 over-mask 比例 rho，把更多 response token 临时 mask 掉，得到候选集合 C。随后从 C 中选择一部分 token reveal 回 gold token，剩余 token S 才作为监督目标。关键点在于 reveal selection 不是随机的。第一次无梯度前向在 over-masked 输入上计算每个候选 token 的 gold-token probability，并抽取最后 attention block 的 attention 作为 token 间支持关系。论文给每个潜在监督 token 分配 priority，偏向 gold-token probability 处在中间区间的 token：太容易的 token 训练收益小，太难且模型几乎没有响应的 token 也可能只带来噪声；中间区域同时有可学习性和剩余提升空间。然后用 attention 估计 reveal token 对其他 masked targets 的支持，并加入 diminishing returns，避免把预算集中在重复提供同类上下文的位置。因为 reveal 一个 token 会增加其他 token 的上下文，但也会失去该 token 自身作为监督目标的机会，这个目标函数是非单调 submodular set selection。选好 reveal set 后进行第二次前向，在新的部分可见上下文下计算剩余 targets 的 gold-token probability。loss weighting 根据 probability 的提升和更新后的置信度来分配：如果某个 token 在获得选中上下文后变得更可学，并且仍有监督空间，就给更高权重。权重会 cap 并归一化，使 supervised positions 的平均权重保持为 1，避免少数 token 吸走过多 loss mass。与只调 mask rate、只按 entropy/position 选 reveal、或只重加权 loss 的方法相比，GoldiMask 的区别是把 context selection 和 target weighting 放在同一个样本级预算里联合处理。32:T5ca,GoldiMask uses a two-pass SFT procedure. For a prompt-response pair, the prompt remains visible and only response tokens are maskable. The method first samples a noise level and over-masks the response, creating a candidate set of masked positions. It then selects a subset to reveal back to their gold tokens, leaving the rest as supervised targets. The first forward pass, run without gradients, estimates each candidate token's gold-token probability and attention-based support relations between positions. Target priority favors intermediate gold-token probabilities: tokens that are already easy carry little training value, while tokens that are too unlikely may provide weak or noisy learning signal. Reveal selection scores how much a revealed token supports the remaining masked targets, with diminishing returns, while accounting for the cost of losing the revealed token as a target. This produces a non-monotone submodular set-selection problem. After selecting the reveal set, a second forward pass evaluates the remaining masked targets under the selected context. Loss weights are increased for tokens whose gold-token probability improves and whose updated confidence still indicates useful supervision. The weights are capped and normalized so that the average supervised-token weight remains one. Compared with methods that only tune masking rate, reveal policy, or token loss weights, GoldiMask treats context selection and target weighting as coupled decisions.33:T4e1,The approach starts by decomposing the RoPE attention score into frequency channels while allowing unequal query-key scales across channels. High-frequency components rotate rapidly with relative distance. They support fine positional changes, but they also introduce fluctuations that can reverse semantic preferences. Low-frequency components preserve smoother content preferences, but they change too little under a one-token shift and can weaken adjacent-position discrimination. The theory turns these two effects into measurable criteria: semantic reversal and positional insensitivity. Under calibrated windows and margin assumptions, it also derives a context-length bound Mmax beyond which a fixed attention margin cannot avoid both failures simultaneously. The empirical tool, RoPE Profiler, reuses cached query/key activations during evaluation and reports two metrics: Semantic Score for preference stability and Positional Score for adjacent-position sensitivity. The proposed interventions are training-free: rescale high-frequency components or freeze their rotations to reduce position-induced fluctuations. This differs from uniform scaling methods because the intervention is guided by per-head and per-input spectral measurements.34:T937,方法很直接，但抓住了问题的结构。论文从 Fast-dLLM 这类 confidence-threshold sampler 出发：每一步对所有 masked positions 预测 token，并计算所采样 token 的 confidence；若某些位置置信度超过阈值 λ，就并行提交这些 token；若没有任何位置超过阈值，则进入 fallback，只提交最高置信的一个位置。作者的观察是，fallback step 恰好是“当前剩余位置都不够确定”的时刻，而这往往与 fork position 尚未被解析有关。因此不必全程 AR，只需在 fallback step 上采用 AR-style ordering。

Fork-dLLM 的具体做法是：在普通步骤完全沿用 Fast-dLLM，继续并行提交所有高置信 token；只有在 fallback step，不再提交最高置信位置，而是提交最左侧的 masked position。这样做的含义是，在模型自己也承认“没有明显高置信位置”时，强制用左到右顺序先决定更早的分叉点，避免后续上下文先被填满、再反过来压缩前面分支的不确定性。它不需要额外前向，也不引入新的阈值或调度规则，改动只发生在 fallback 的位置选择上。

论文还分析了为什么这能改善 pass@k。confidence-based sampler 的问题不是并行本身，而是它倾向于先解那些“容易的、后验已接近确定”的位置，导致真正决定程序分支、证明路径或长程语义走向的位置被拖到很后面。等这些位置终于被采样时，周围上下文已经被大量提交，分支空间被上下文收缩，多个样本会收敛到相似 continuation。Fork-dLLM 在不确定步骤上恢复局部 AR，等于在最需要保留分支自由度的时候，优先决定早期位置。

ForkGRPO 则把同样的思想搬到 RL。dLLM 做 policy gradient/GRPO 的难点在于，一次并行提交多个 token 时，精确的 trajectory likelihood ratio 不再像 AR 那样容易分解。已有避免近似的方法通常直接用 AR rollout。ForkGRPO 的做法是：rollout 仍按 Fork-dLLM 生成，但只在 fallback steps 应用 GRPO objective。因为这些步骤每次只提交一个 token，所以该步的 policy-likelihood ratio 是精确可算的；而非 fallback steps 继续享受并行生成带来的低 NFE。这样在目标函数层面保住了 exact ratio，在采样层面保住了大部分并行性。35:T8f3,The method is simple, but it targets the right structural point. The starting point is a Fast-dLLM-style confidence-threshold sampler. At each step, the model predicts candidate tokens for all masked positions and assigns each sampled token a confidence score. Positions above a threshold λ are committed in parallel. If no position exceeds the threshold, the sampler enters a fallback mode and commits a single position so that progress continues.

The key observation is that fallback steps already identify moments of global uncertainty: no remaining position looks confidently resolvable. Those are precisely the steps where unresolved fork positions are likely to matter. Fork-dLLM therefore keeps the original confidence-based parallel behavior on ordinary steps, but changes the fallback rule. Instead of committing the highest-confidence position, it commits the leftmost masked position, i.e., an AR-style choice. This means the sampler only restores left-to-right ordering when the model itself signals that parallel confidence-based commitment is no longer reliable.

Why does this help? The issue with confidence-based decoding is not parallelism per se. The issue is that it tends to fill in easy, already-nearly-determined positions first, while delaying the positions that determine program branches, proof paths, or semantically meaningful continuations. By the time those fork positions are finally sampled, surrounding context has already collapsed much of the branching space, so different samples become too similar. Fork-dLLM intervenes exactly at those uncertain moments and resolves earlier positions first, preserving diversity where it matters most.

ForkGRPO extends the same idea to RL post-training. In dLLMs, exact trajectory likelihood ratios become awkward when multiple tokens are committed in parallel at one step. Existing methods that avoid approximations often fall back to AR rollouts. ForkGRPO instead generates rollouts with Fork-dLLM and applies the GRPO objective only at fallback steps. Since each fallback step commits exactly one token, the policy-likelihood ratio at that step is exact. Non-fallback steps still benefit from parallel generation. This gives a clean compromise: exact ratios where they are tractable, parallelism where it is safe.36:T663,The main empirical results concern pass@k scaling and RL efficiency. On mathematics and coding benchmarks, Fork-dLLM matches the pass@k scaling of autoregressive sampling while requiring only about one-half to one-third as many NFEs, i.e., roughly a 2–3x reduction in model evaluations. That is the central inference result: escaping the flexibility trap does not require turning a dLLM into a fully AR generator. The paper also shows that, with proper tuning, other confidence-based samplers can retain strong pass@k behavior at a fraction of AR cost, reinforcing the claim that the problem lies in the decoding policy rather than in parallel unmasking itself.

For RL post-training, ForkGRPO is compared against AR-based GRPO under matched compute budgets. The reported outcome is that ForkGRPO clearly outperforms the AR-based baseline when compute is fixed, and can match it at a substantially lower training cost. The gain comes from both sides: fewer NFEs during rollout generation and fewer exact-ratio optimization steps because the objective is applied only on fallback steps. The abstract does not list the full numeric tables, but Figure 1 and Section 4.2 make the qualitative result clear.

The most interesting ablation insight is the effectiveness of fallback steps as a proxy for fork-containing steps. The method does not explicitly detect branch points and does not train an auxiliary classifier. It simply reuses an event already present in Fast-dLLM decoding: no position exceeds the confidence threshold. The experiments suggest that this proxy is good enough to capture the moments that drive diversity collapse.37:T536,Read this paper in three passes. First, read the introduction and background to internalize the mechanism of the flexibility trap. The important point is not merely that confidence-based decoding hurts diversity, but why: it systematically postpones the uncertain branch-defining positions. Second, read Algorithm 2 and its surrounding explanation carefully. The modification is tiny, but the choice of the leftmost masked position at fallback is the conceptual core. It is not adding a little AR for its own sake; it is restoring causal ordering only when uncertainty is high.

Third, read Section 3.2 on ForkGRPO if you care about the pretrain-to-posttrain interface or RL for non-AR models. That section addresses a practical obstacle for diffusion LMs in RL: how to preserve exact policy ratios without making the whole rollout autoregressive. If you work on diffusion LMs, any-order generation, or RL for reasoning, the appendix discussion on likelihood approximations and why the objective is restricted to fallback steps is worth the extra time.38:T727,NAMOH 将每个 attention head 视为一个 expert。对每个 token，router 从总共 H 个 heads 中选择 top-K 个 active heads。关键点是 routing 不只决定哪些 head 参数参与计算，也决定每个 head 保存哪些 token。每个 head 只在被分配到自己的 token 子序列上做 causal attention，而不是先构造完整 attention 再做稀疏 mask。这样稀疏性来自架构路由结构。论文使用 load balancing 防止 tokens 都被路由到少数 heads，目标是在 H 个 heads 上近似均匀分配。若上下文长度为 L，每个 token 激活 K 个 heads，总 KV 条目数约为 LK；在均衡路由下，每个 head 约保存 LK/H 个 token。一个 query 会访问 K 个 active heads，各 head 中约 LK/H 个 KV，因此每 token 访问约 LK^2/H 个 KV。相对同 active attention 参数的 K-head full attention，KV activation ratio 约为 K/H；相对同 total attention 参数的 H-head full attention，约为 (K/H)^2。论文给出的例子是 H=32、K=8，总 KV 存储为 32-head full attention 的 1/4，与 8-head full attention 相同；每个 active token 访问的 KV 约为 2L，对应相对 32-head full attention 的 1/16 activation ratio，相对 8-head full attention 的 1/4。另一个重要设计是 head-relative RoPE：位置不按全局序列位置编码，而按 token 在对应 head 子序列中的相对位置编码。这样 RoPE 编码跨度从 L 缩到约 LK/H，同时保留顺序信息，目标是减轻长 RoPE span 下的 query-key 偶然对齐和位置噪声。实现上，训练和 prefill 通过 variable-length FlashAttention 打包各 head 子序列；decoding 时只执行 active heads 的 query，并且只读写这些 heads 的 KV cache。论文还指出该方法可以和 GQA、已有 sparse attention 的 token/block selection 叠加。39:T741,NAMOH treats each attention head as an expert. For every token, a learned router selects the top-K heads out of H total heads. Routing has two roles: it activates the selected head parameters, and it assigns tokens to the corresponding head-specific subsequences. Each head then performs causal attention only within its own routed subsequence. Sparsity is therefore native to the architecture, rather than being imposed by masking a dense attention computation. A load-balancing objective is used to avoid head collapse and to keep token assignments roughly uniform. With sequence length L, total KV entries are about LK. Under balanced routing, each head stores around LK/H entries, and a query accessing K active heads reads about LK^2/H KV entries. Relative to a K-head full-attention baseline with matched active attention parameters, the KV activation ratio is about K/H. Relative to an H-head full-attention baseline with matched total attention parameters, it is about (K/H)^2. For H=32 and K=8, total KV storage is one quarter of 32-head full attention and equal to 8-head full attention; each active query reads around 2L KV entries, giving activation ratios of 1/16 versus 32-head full attention and 1/4 versus 8-head full attention. The paper also introduces head-relative RoPE, where positions are encoded within each head’s routed subsequence rather than by global token index. This shortens the effective positional span to roughly LK/H while preserving order, aiming to reduce long-RoPE attention noise. Implementation-wise, training and prefill use packed variable-length FlashAttention over head-specific subsequences, while decoding only runs active heads and only reads or updates their KV caches. The design is described as compatible with GQA and with additional token- or block-level sparse attention inside each routed subsequence.3a:T902,作者先给出一个统一的 distributional distillation 公式：把 student 生成的样本经过 embedding 和 Gaussian noising，得到 noised student distribution；再与真实数据对应的 noised data distribution 做某种 discrepancy matching。这个框架可以覆盖已有一些方法，也能自然扩展到 multi-step generation。论文随后把 discrepancy 特化为 reverse KL，并在同一 student 架构下推导出两条路线。

第一条是 Simplex-DMD。student 在每个位置直接输出词表上的概率向量，把它视作 simplex 上的连续 token relaxation，再映射到 embedding 空间并加噪。由于整个路径是连续可导的，可以使用 pathwise gradients。为了估计 noised student distribution 的 score，方法引入一个 auxiliary denoiser，思路延续了 Diff-Instruct / DMD 一类 continuous-data distribution matching 方法，但这里适配的是离散文本经 simplex relaxation 后的连续表示。它的优点是低步数下训练和采样都更稳定，缺点是 relaxation 可能带来偏差，尤其在高质量、低熵文本区域会受限。

第二条是 Reinforce-DMD。这里 student 仍输出 categorical distribution，但训练时从中采样离散 token，再 embedding、加噪，并通过 REINFORCE 估计梯度。为了构造 reverse-KL 所需的密度比，作者训练一个 discriminator 来估计 noised student 与 noised data 之间的 density ratio。这样做避免了 simplex relaxation 的连续近似偏差，更贴近真正的离散生成分布，但代价是方差更高、训练更难，需要更仔细的稳定化设计。论文还把两种方法都扩展到 multi-step generation，而不是只做 one-step distillation，这一点很关键，因为语言生成质量通常对少量中间 refinement step 很敏感。

和已有 trajectory-based distillation 不同，这里不要求 student 追随 teacher 的具体去噪轨迹，而是直接匹配最终分布。这种做法给 student 更大自由度，也更适合研究不同输出参数化下的质量-多样性权衡。论文的一个重要观察是：同样是 reverse-KL matching，不同参数化在不同 NFE 区间各有优势，说明“最佳蒸馏方法”并不存在统一答案，而是取决于你想把采样预算压到多低。3b:T918,The paper starts from a unified distributional distillation view. Student samples are embedded and noised, producing a noised student distribution, which is then matched to the corresponding noised data distribution through a generic discrepancy. This formulation subsumes prior distribution-matching approaches and extends naturally to multi-step generation. The authors then specialize the discrepancy to reverse KL and derive two methods under the same student architecture.

Simplex-DMD keeps the student outputs as probability vectors over the vocabulary. These are treated as continuous simplex-valued token relaxations, embedded, and corrupted with Gaussian noise. Because the whole path is differentiable, training can use pathwise gradients. To estimate the score of the noised student distribution, the method introduces an auxiliary denoiser, in the spirit of DMD and Diff-Instruct, but adapted to discrete text represented through continuous simplex relaxations. This route is attractive at very low sampling budgets because it is relatively stable and efficient, though it may suffer from approximation bias due to the relaxation.

Reinforce-DMD instead samples categorical tokens from the student distributions, then embeds and noises those discrete samples. Gradients are estimated with REINFORCE, and a discriminator is trained to estimate the density ratio between the noised student and noised data distributions, which is needed for the reverse-KL objective. This avoids the bias introduced by continuous relaxations and stays closer to the true discrete generation process, but it pays with higher variance and more delicate optimization. Importantly, both methods are extended to multi-step generation rather than only one-step distillation, which matters because language quality is often sensitive to a small number of refinement steps.

A notable design choice is the use of distribution matching rather than trajectory matching. The student is not forced to imitate the teacher’s denoising path. It only needs to match the target distribution. That gives the student more freedom and makes the comparison between parameterizations cleaner. One of the paper’s main findings is exactly that there is no universally best parameterization: the preferred method depends strongly on the target NFE regime.3c:T5c8,The experiments distill the same 170M-parameter LangFlow teacher on OpenWebText and evaluate 1,024-token generation. Instead of reporting only a single perplexity number, the paper uses generative perplexity–entropy frontiers, which is the right choice here because it exposes the quality-diversity trade-off rather than rewarding collapsed distributions.

The main empirical result is a clear complementarity between the two methods. Simplex-DMD is stronger in the low-NFE regime, especially at 2–16 network evaluations. A representative number is at 4 NFEs and unigram entropy 5.44, where Simplex-DMD achieves Gen PPL 45.6 versus 90.2 for ReDi. Reinforce-DMD becomes stronger at higher budgets. At 256 NFEs and entropy 5.00, it improves Gen PPL from 18.6 for D-MMD to 14.9, and at 128 NFEs it already matches the best baseline. This pattern aligns with the method design: continuous relaxations help when the budget is extremely tight, while discrete sampling with REINFORCE better preserves the true discrete distribution when more refinement steps are available.

The paper also studies multi-step training choices and sampling decisions, framing the results in terms of quality-diversity trade-offs rather than a single scalar score. Even from the available content, the key message is clear: the student output parameterization is not a minor implementation detail. It determines the estimator, the optimization behavior, and the shape of the final performance frontier.3d:T590,Read this one with a specific question in mind: what exactly is being matched, and how does the student representation change the estimator? While reading, keep asking what bias is introduced by the simplex relaxation and where the variance enters in the REINFORCE route.

In the experiments, prioritize the generative perplexity–entropy frontiers rather than isolated point metrics.
